questions.q: What did bulimia and heavy drinking provide for Glennon in her early years?
a: A hiding place where she could avoid confronting her problems
A reliable route to academic and professional success
A close circle of friends who supported her recovery
A way to strengthen her marriage before it began
questions.why: Lesson 1 says her eating disorder and drinking became a hiding place from problems until everything collapsed.

questions.q: What did Glennon finally start doing after she learned about Craig’s affairs?
a: Listening to the inner voice she had silenced for most of her life
Leaving her marriage immediately and cutting off all contact
Returning to bulimia as a way of coping with the betrayal
Giving up writing because she feared public judgment
questions.why: Lesson 2 describes how, with nothing left to lose, she began listening to her inner voice and writing.

questions.q: According to the summary, what is the purest form of authenticity and self-love?
a: Knowing and accepting pain as part of being human
Avoiding vulnerability so others cannot hurt you
Building a public persona that hides your flaws
Pleasing everyone around you at all costs
questions.why: Lesson 3 argues that accepting pain acknowledges your humanity and lets you own all parts of yourself.

questions.q: What happened when Glennon began writing openly about her pain?
a: Her honesty resonated online and created a space where women felt less alone
She was criticized so harshly that she stopped publishing her writing
She became famous but felt more isolated than before
Her blog only reached a small group of personal friends
questions.why: Lesson 3 says her blog became an online sensation and a judgment-free space for women sharing struggles.

questions.q: What did Glennon realize marriage, a loving husband and children could not do?
a: Make her healthy again or resolve her underlying struggles
Give her a sense of purpose or daily routine
Provide the motivation to write about her experiences
Help her understand the pain of other women
questions.why: Lesson 1 notes that after marrying she saw none of these could make her healthy; recovery was her own work.
